report: # 1. Executive Diagnosis + Summary of Reason IIMK_PCPF_10 is **mixed**: it exceeded every available volume and GSV plan, but materially underperformed all three historical batches on applications, enrollments, most conversion rates, and observed-spend acquisition efficiency. Actual GSV reached ₹1.248 crore, 55.0% above plan, but remained below each prior batch despite the higher ₹240,000 program fee. - Leads were 4,260 versus 2,455 planned, exceeding plan by 73.5%. - Applications and enrollments exceeded plan by 60.0% and 48.6%, respectively. - Actual GSV was ₹12.48 million versus ₹8.05 million planned, a positive variance of ₹4.43 million. - Observed spend was ₹2.73 million, 46.3% above the ₹1.87 million planned budget. - Applications were 25.6%–34.7% below the three prior batches; enrollments were 27.8%–37.3% lower. - Observed-spend CPL was 15.2%–33.2% higher and CAC was 53.3%–92.8% higher than prior batches. ## Where it went wrong 1. **Historical volumes weakened despite beating plan.** Applications were 64 versus 40 planned, but below IIMK_PCPF_09, _08, and _07 by 24 (-27.3%), 22 (-25.6%), and 34 (-34.7%), respectively. Enrollments showed the same pattern: 52 versus 35 planned, but down 20 (-27.8%), 24 (-31.6%), and 31 (-37.3%). 2. **The main funnel leakage was before application.** L2A was 1.50%, down 0.41 pp versus _09, 0.12 pp versus _08, and 0.91 pp versus _07. W2A fell to 4.73%, down 1.16 pp, 1.07 pp, and 1.87 pp, respectively; therefore, weaker warm-lead-to-application progression is an observed contributor, while the underlying cause is not available. 3. **Lead warming was not uniformly worse, but did not translate into applications.** L2W was 31.78%: down 0.71 pp versus _09 and 4.80 pp versus _07, but up 3.85 pp versus _08. This indicates that lead volume or warming alone does not explain the lower application output. 4. **Acquisition efficiency deteriorated while spend exceeded budget.** Observed spend was ₹2.73 million versus ₹1.87 million planned, an overrun of ₹863,264 or 46.3%. Observed-spend CPL increased 19.7%, 33.2%, and 15.2% versus _09, _08, and _07; CAC increased 53.3%, 56.1%, and 92.8%. 5. **Ratings:** - **Plan attainment rating: Good — 100.0%.** Included metrics: leads, applications, enrollments, and GSV. Their raw attainments were 173.5%, 160.0%, 148.6%, and 155.0%; each was capped at 100% for scoring. - **Historical comparison rating: Poor.** Against _09: **0 improved / 10 declined / 0 unchanged**; against _08: **1 improved / 9 declined / 0 unchanged**; against _07: **1 improved / 9 declined / 0 unchanged**. Direction-aware comparisons cover leads, applications, enrollments, five conversion rates, CPL, and CAC. # 2. Source-wise root-cause analysis Lead volume exceeded plan, but source quality and progression varied materially. Facebook generated 2,158 leads—50.7% of total leads—but only six applications and two enrollments, with the lowest material-volume L2A and L2E at 0.28% and 0.09%. Google produced the most enrollments at 15 and a 3.13% L2A, but its observed-spend CPL and CAC were ₹2,259 and ₹96,399. Website and referral had the highest conversion rates, but their small lead bases and unavailable spend prevent scalable efficiency conclusions. Observed spend is available only for Google, LinkedIn, and Facebook at source level; therefore, source cost comparisons are incomplete. The 07–12 month group handled the largest volume—1,712 leads—but ranked fourth with a 12.79% score, making it the largest-volume improvement opportunity. These are associations only; the evidence does not establish that tenure caused the observed performance. # 6. Prioritized actions 1. **Address Facebook funnel leakage first.** Review lead qualification, campaign targeting, and warm-lead follow-up for the 2,158 Facebook leads, given its 0.28% L2A, 0.09% L2E, and observed-spend CAC of ₹418,010.50. 2. **Improve warm-lead-to-application progression.** Audit contact cadence, application assistance, and disposition outcomes across sources because W2A declined by 1.07–1.87 pp versus every historical batch. The evidence identifies the stage of leakage, but not its operational cause. 3. **Protect higher-converting source pathways.** Evaluate whether website, referral, Others, and database practices can be replicated, while recognizing their smaller volumes and unavailable source spend. Finance and Marketing should validate full cost attribution before reallocating budget. 4. **Review high-volume advisor cohorts.** Prioritize coaching and workflow review for the 07–12 and 24+ tenure groups, which together handled 2,426 leads but recorded L2E of 0.99% and 0.84%. Validate lead-source and lead-quality mix before attributing differences to advisor tenure. 5. **Reconcile the budget overrun and observed-spend efficiency.** Finance should validate the ₹863,264 variance against planned budget and confirm whether all spend categories are included consistently across batches. Marketing should then assess whether the higher spend produced incremental qualified demand, as the available evidence shows weaker historical CPL and CAC but cannot establish the cause.
